newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Portugal copper strikers to make new bid for talks.
newsitem.headline: Portugal copper strikers to make new bid for talks.

text.p: Striking Portuguese copper miners were to meet on Friday afternoon to discuss a fresh approach to management on a proposal that could put an end to the five-day stoppage, a senior official said.

Eduardo Lazaro told Reuters that union officials would propose that the controversial issue of Sunday working, the question that triggered the strike, be resolved by making it voluntary while negotiations continued with the company on a permanent solution.
If the company agreed to the proposal, the unions would recommend a return to work, he said.
Union officials told Reuters that the miners' meeting should start around 1400 GMT.
Miners have been on strike at the 107,000 tonne per year Neves Corvo copper mine since Monday in protest at the company's insistence on Sunday working.
Talks with management, which argues that existing work contracts allow for Sunday working, have so far always ended in deadlock.
The mine, which is run by state-owned Somincor, says that operations need to be maintained seven days a week for the producer to remain competitive.
